The literal complete exponential resummation is nonzero in the original L2
space and has mean Gamma(s-1). Every actual Xi target differs from the native
constant eigenvalue one. The exact mean identity for the actual covariance
therefore gives a nonzero full source residual, with a quantitative norm bound.

The admitted source cannot be an entire eigenvector at its common scalar term
value. Applying the actual covariance constructs a nonzero entire-domain vector
whose normalized full-Xi residual is strictly positive. Exact centering isolates
the remaining source equation without asserting its solution or nonvanishing.
-/

open Set Filter Topology MeasureTheory UpperHalfPlane
open GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry
open scoped InnerProductSpace
namespace RHTower.SelbergResummedOccurrenceAudit
open D4BMModularCore D4BMGlobalAngularResponse SelbergResummedSource SelbergNativeConstantMode
open SelbergScatteringEntireOperator SelbergScatteringEntireTransform SelbergScatteringEntireXiPackets
noncomputable section

/-- An actual Xi target never equals the original constant-mode eigenvalue. -/
theorem xiEntireTarget_ne_one (q : XiZeroCopy) : xiEntireTarget q ≠ 1 := by
  intro he
  have hp : casimirTransform (0:ℝ) = xiEntireTarget q := by
    rw [he]
    exact casimirTransform_zero
  have h := ((xi_real_native_preimage_iff q 0).mp hp).2
  dsimp [nativePartner] at h
  nlinarith [sq_nonneg (q.1:ℂ).im]

/-- The exact mean belongs to the original resummed native vector. -/
theorem xiVector_integral (q : XiZeroCopy) :
    (∫ z, (xiVector q) z ∂measure) = Complex.Gamma (xiParameter q-1) := by
  rw [integral_congr_ae (xiVector_coe q)]
  exact source_integral_eq_gamma _ (xiParameter_strip q).1 (xiParameter_strip q).2

/-- Complete bounded occurrence residual for the actual resummed Xi source. -/
def sourceDefect (q : XiZeroCopy) : Space := boundedDefect (xiEntireTarget q) (xiVector q)

/-- The complete residual has an explicit, non-discarded original mean. -/
theorem sourceDefect_integral (q : XiZeroCopy) :
    (∫ z, (sourceDefect q) z ∂measure) =
      ((1-xiEntireTarget q)/3)*Complex.Gamma (xiParameter q-1) := by
  rw [sourceDefect,integral_boundedDefect,xiVector_integral]

/-- Local resummation creates an admitted nonzero source but leaves a nonzero occurrence defect. -/
theorem sourceDefect_ne_zero (q : XiZeroCopy) : sourceDefect q ≠ 0 :=
  boundedDefect_ne_zero_of_integral_ne_zero _ (xiEntireTarget_ne_one q) _
    (xiVector_integral_ne_zero q)

/-- Exact quantitative lower demand on the full source residual. -/
theorem sourceDefect_norm_lower (q : XiZeroCopy) :
    ‖1-xiEntireTarget q‖*‖Complex.Gamma (xiParameter q-1)‖ ≤
      3*‖constantVector‖*‖sourceDefect q‖ := by
  simpa only [xiVector_integral,sourceDefect] using boundedDefect_norm_lower (xiEntireTarget q) (xiVector q)

/-- The admitted original vector cannot be an entire eigenvector at its shared scalar term value. -/
theorem xiVector_not_entire_eigenvector (q : XiZeroCopy) :
    ¬ ∃ x : entireOperator.domain, (x:Space)=xiVector q ∧
      entireOperator x = xiEntireTarget q • (x:Space) := by
  rintro ⟨x,hx,hT⟩
  have h := entireCovariance_apply_operator x
  rw [hT,hx,map_add,map_smul,map_smul] at h
  apply sourceDefect_ne_zero q
  unfold sourceDefect boundedDefect
  have he : (2+xiEntireTarget q) • entireCovariance (xiVector q) = xiVector q := by
    rw [add_smul,add_comm]
    exact h
  rw [he,sub_self]

/-- Applying the actual covariance constructs a source in the full native entire graph. -/
def domainSource (q : XiZeroCopy) : entireOperator.domain :=
  ⟨entireCovariance (xiVector q),entireCovariance_mem_domain _⟩

theorem domainSource_ne_zero (q : XiZeroCopy) : (domainSource q : Space) ≠ 0 := by
  intro he
  apply xiVector_ne_zero q
  apply entireCovariance_injective
  simpa [domainSource] using he

/-- The actual domain source has the same complete bounded defect as its literal operator residual. -/
theorem domainSource_operator_defect (q : XiZeroCopy) :
    entireOperator (domainSource q)-xiEntireTarget q • (domainSource q : Space) = sourceDefect q := by
  change entireOperator ⟨entireCovariance (xiVector q),entireCovariance_mem_domain _⟩ -
    xiEntireTarget q • entireCovariance (xiVector q) = _
  rw [entireOperator_apply_covariance]
  unfold sourceDefect boundedDefect
  module

/-- The actual native entire-domain source has strictly positive normalized full-Xi residual. -/
theorem domainSource_normalized_residual_pos (q : XiZeroCopy) :
    0 < ‖entireOperator (domainSource q)-xiEntireTarget q • (domainSource q : Space)‖ /
      ‖(domainSource q : Space)‖ := by
  rw [domainSource_operator_defect]
  exact div_pos (norm_pos_iff.mpr (sourceDefect_ne_zero q)) (norm_pos_iff.mpr (domainSource_ne_zero q))

's actual native mean. -/
theorem xi_source_integral_ne_zero (q : XiZeroCopy) :
    (∫ z, source (xiParameter q) z ∂angularMeasure) ≠ 0 :=
  source_integral_ne_zero _ (xiParameter_strip q).1 (xiParameter_strip q).2

/-- The admitted original Hilbert vector, obtained after full local resummation. -/
def xiVector (q : XiZeroCopy) : Space := (xi_source_memLp q).toLp (source (xiParameter q))

theorem xiVector_coe (q : XiZeroCopy) : (xiVector q : UpperHalfPlane → ℂ) =ᵐ[angularMeasure]
    source (xiParameter q) := (xi_source_memLp q).coeFn_toLp

/-- Nonzero native mass belongs to the actual resummed vector. -/
theorem xiVector_integral_ne_zero (q : XiZeroCopy) :
    (∫ z, (xiVector q : UpperHalfPlane → ℂ) z ∂angularMeasure) ≠ 0 := by
  rw [integral_congr_ae (xiVector_coe q)]
  exact xi_source_integral_ne_zero q

theorem xiVector_ne_zero (q : XiZeroCopy) : xiVector q ≠ 0 := by
  intro he
  have h := xiVector_integral_ne_zero q
  rw [he,integral_congr_ae (Lp.coeFn_zero ℂ 2 angularMeasure)] at h
  exact h (by simp)

end
end RHTower.SelbergResummedSource

/-!
# Two bounds on mean squares

The mean square of a bounded function is at most the square of its sup norm, and the mean square of
the spectral partial sum is at most the mean square of the function — the latter being Bessel's
inequality read through the mean square of a trigonometric polynomial.

Both are needed to turn a mean-square approximation into a bound on the coefficients of a product.
-/

open MeasureTheory ComplexConjugate

open scoped BoundedContinuousFunction

namespace GaloisForLFunctions

open HTGeometry

noncomputable section

/-- The mean square is at most the squared sup norm. -/
theorem bohrMean_mul_conj_re_le_norm_sq {f : ℝ →ᵇ ℂ}
    (hap : IsBohrAlmostPeriodic (fun x => f x)) :
    (bohrMean (fun t => f t * conj (f t))).re ≤ ‖f‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) := by
  have hcont : Continuous (fun x => f x) := f.continuous
  have hc : Continuous fun t : ℝ => (f : ℝ → ℂ) t * conj ((f : ℝ → ℂ) t) :=
    hcont.mul (Complex.continuous_conj.comp hcont)
  have ha : IsBohrAlmostPeriodic fun t : ℝ => (f : ℝ → ℂ) t * conj ((f : ℝ → ℂ) t) :=
    isBohrAlmostPeriodic_mul hcont hap (Complex.continuous_conj.comp hcont)
      (isBohrAlmostPeriodic_conj hap)
  refine le_trans (Complex.re_le_norm _) ?_
  refine norm_bohrMean_le hc ha fun t => ?_
  rw [norm_mul, RCLike.norm_conj, ← pow_two]
  exact pow_le_pow_left₀ (norm_nonneg _) (f.norm_coe_le_norm t) 2

/-- **Bessel's inequality in mean-square form.**  The spectral partial sum has mean square at most
that of the function. -/
theorem bohrMean_trigPoly_mul_conj_self_re_le {f : ℝ →ᵇ ℂ}
    (hap : IsBohrAlmostPeriodic (fun x => f x)) (S : Finset ℝ) :
    (bohrMean (fun t => trigPoly S (bohrCoefficient (fun x => f x)) t *
      conj (trigPoly S (bohrCoefficient (fun x => f x)) t))).re
      ≤ (bohrMean (fun t => f t * conj (f t))).re := by
  have hval := bohrMean_trigPoly_mul_conj_self S (bohrCoefficient (fun x => f x))
  rw [hval, Complex.re_sum]
  have hterm : ∀ lam ∈ S, (bohrCoefficient (fun x => f x) lam *
      conj (bohrCoefficient (fun x => f x) lam)).re
      = ‖bohrCoefficient (fun x => f x) lam‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) := by
    intro lam _
    rw [Complex.mul_conj']
    norm_cast
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl hterm]
  exact bohr_bessel f.continuous hap S

end

end GaloisForLFunctions

/-!
# The mean-square floor of a normalized detector

A detector Dirichlet polynomial whose first coefficient is `1` has coefficient energy at least `1`,
so the mean value theorem forces its window mean square to be at least the window length minus the
mean-value error.  Normalized by the window length the mean square is therefore at least `1 - ε`
once the window is long compared with the error, and `log` of the normalized mean square is at least
`log (1 - ε)`.

This is a floor, not an estimate: no choice of mollifier can push the normalized mean square of a
detector with leading coefficient `1` below `1`.  In the off-line displacement chain the mean square
enters through `(T₂ - T₁)/2 · log (Msq / (T₂ - T₁))`, so that term is bounded below by
`(T₂ - T₁)/2 · log (1 - ε)` and can never supply the negativity needed to force the
multiplicity-weighted horizontal displacement to vanish.
-/

open Finset MeasureTheory intervalIntegral

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- A normalized coefficient family has energy at least one. -/
theorem one_le_coeff_energy {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (a : Fin N → ℂ) (ha : a ⟨0, hN⟩ = 1) :
    (1 : ℝ) ≤ ∑ m : Fin N, ‖a m‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) := by
  have hterm : ‖a (⟨0, hN⟩ : Fin N)‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) = 1 := by
    rw [ha]
    simp
  calc (1 : ℝ) = ‖a (⟨0, hN⟩ : Fin N)‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) := hterm.symm
    _ ≤ ∑ m : Fin N, ‖a m‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) :=
        Finset.single_le_sum (f := fun m : Fin N => ‖a m‖ ^ (2 : ℕ))
          (fun m _ => by positivity) (Finset.mem_univ _)

/-- **The mean-square floor.**  A detector with leading coefficient `1` has window mean square at
least the window length minus the mean-value error. -/
theorem dirPoly_meanSquare_floor {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (a : Fin N → ℂ) (ha : a ⟨0, hN⟩ = 1)
    {T₁ T₂ : ℝ} (hT : T₁ ≤ T₂) :
    (T₂ - T₁) - 8 * (N : ℝ) * (1 + Real.log N)
      ≤ ∫ t in T₁..T₂, ‖Sieve.dirPoly N a t‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) := by
  have hS1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ ∑ m : Fin N, ‖a m‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) := one_le_coeff_energy hN a ha
  have hlogN : 0 ≤ Real.log N := Real.log_natCast_nonneg N
  have hN0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) := Nat.cast_nonneg N
  have hC : 0 ≤ 8 * (N : ℝ) * (1 + Real.log N) := by positivity
  have hmvt := Sieve.dirichlet_meanValue_window N a T₁ T₂
  have hlow : (T₂ - T₁) * (∑ m : Fin N, ‖a m‖ ^ (2 : ℕ))
        - 8 * (N : ℝ) * (1 + Real.log N) * (∑ m : Fin N, ‖a m‖ ^ (2 : ℕ))
      ≤ ∫ t in T₁..T₂, ‖Sieve.dirPoly N a t‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) := by
    have habs := abs_le.mp hmvt
    linarith [habs.1]
  have hnonneg : 0 ≤ ∫ t in T₁..T₂, ‖Sieve.dirPoly N a t‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) :=
    intervalIntegral.integral_nonneg hT (fun t _ => by positivity)
  rcases le_or_gt (8 * (N : ℝ) * (1 + Real.log N)) (T₂ - T₁) with hcase | hcase
  · have hfac : (T₂ - T₁) - 8 * (N : ℝ) * (1 + Real.log N)
        ≤ ((T₂ - T₁) - 8 * (N : ℝ) * (1 + Real.log N)) * (∑ m : Fin N, ‖a m‖ ^ (2 : ℕ)) := by
      nlinarith [hS1, hcase]
    nlinarith [hlow, hfac]
  · linarith [hnonneg, hcase]

/-- The normalized mean square is at least `1 - ε` on a window long compared with the
mean-value error. -/
theorem one_sub_mul_le_dirPoly_meanSquare {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (a : Fin N → ℂ)
    (ha : a ⟨0, hN⟩ = 1) {ε T₁ T₂ : ℝ} (hT : T₁ ≤ T₂)
    (hwin : 8 * (N : ℝ) * (1 + Real.log N) ≤ ε * (T₂ - T₁)) :
    (1 - ε) * (T₂ - T₁) ≤ ∫ t in T₁..T₂, ‖Sieve.dirPoly N a t‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) := by
  have h := dirPoly_meanSquare_floor hN a ha hT
  nlinarith [h, hwin]

/-- **The logarithmic floor.**  The logarithm of the normalized mean square is at least
`log (1 - ε)`; it never becomes a useful negative quantity. -/
theorem log_one_sub_le_log_dirPoly_meanSquare_div {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (a : Fin N → ℂ)
    (ha : a ⟨0, hN⟩ = 1) {ε T₁ T₂ : ℝ} (hT : T₁ < T₂) (hε1 : ε < 1)
    (hwin : 8 * (N : ℝ) * (1 + Real.log N) ≤ ε * (T₂ - T₁)) :
    Real.log (1 - ε)
      ≤ Real.log ((∫ t in T₁..T₂, ‖Sieve.dirPoly N a t‖ ^ (2 : ℕ)) / (T₂ - T₁)) := by
  have hD : 0 < T₂ - T₁ := by linarith
  have h := one_sub_mul_le_dirPoly_meanSquare hN a ha hT.le hwin
  have hdiv : 1 - ε ≤ (∫ t in T₁..T₂, ‖Sieve.dirPoly N a t‖ ^ (2 : ℕ)) / (T₂ - T₁) := by
    rw [le_div_iff₀ hD]
    linarith
  exact Real.log_le_log (by linarith) hdiv

end

end RHTower

/-
The frontier object under the large sieve: the mean is exactly right, and only the maximum is open.

The frontier object is `Σ_(r) c_r e(n ξ_r)` over the `R ≍ N^(2/3)` Farey fractions of order
`L = N^(1/3)`, with unimodular coefficients and frequencies `ξ_r = √(2a/q)`.  The dual large sieve
gives

    Σ_(n ≤ N) |Σ_r c_r e(n ξ_r)|²  ≪  (N + δ^(-1)) Σ_r |c_r|² ,

where `δ` is the minimal spacing of the frequencies.  The spacing is `≫ L^(-2) = N^(-2/3)`, so
`δ^(-1) ≪ N^(2/3) ≪ N` and the mean square over `n ≤ N` is `≪ R = N^(2/3)`:

    **root mean square  ≪  N^(1/3)  —  exactly the Lindelöf value.**

So the across-arc half of the cancellation is available *in mean square*, and the entire deficit is
the passage from mean to maximum.  Quantitatively, at most `N^(1-2δ)` of the `N` values of `n` can
have the sum exceed `N^(1/3+δ)`.

On the other side, the resonance method gives a lower bound `≫ N^(1/3) exp(c√(log N log log N))`,
subpolynomially above the Lindelöf value.  So for the frontier object:

    mean square exponent        **2/3**   (root mean square **1/3**)
    known lower bound           **1/3**   up to `exp(c√(log N log log N))`
    trivial upper bound         **2/3**
    Lindelöf assertion          **1/3**

**Every known lower bound sits within a subpolynomial factor of the mean; the whole open interval is
the factor `N^(1/3)` between the mean and the trivial maximum.**
-/
import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.FourAccountings

namespace HTGeometry

/-! ### The sieve input -/

/-- Exponent of the number of Farey fractions of order `N^(1/3)`. -/
def frontierTermCount : ℚ := 2 / 3

/-- Exponent of the minimal spacing of the frontier frequencies (negative). -/
def frontierSpacing : ℚ := -(2 / 3)

/-- **The sieve's second term is dominated by the first.**  `δ^(-1) ≍ N^(2/3)` against `N`. -/
theorem sieve_second_term_negligible : -frontierSpacing < 1 := by
  unfold frontierSpacing; norm_num

/-- **The mean-square exponent delivered by the sieve.** -/
def frontierMeanSquare : ℚ := frontierTermCount

/-- **Its square root is exactly the Lindelöf value.** -/
theorem frontier_rms : frontierMeanSquare / 2 = 1 / 3 := by
  unfold frontierMeanSquare frontierTermCount; norm_num

/-! ### The three levels -/

/-- The trivial bound on the frontier object. -/
def frontierTrivial : ℚ := 2 / 3

/-- The Lindelöf assertion for the frontier object. -/
def frontierLindelof : ℚ := 1 / 3

/-- The root mean square, which the sieve delivers unconditionally. -/
def frontierRootMeanSquare : ℚ := 1 / 3

/-- **The root mean square already equals the Lindelöf value.** -/
theorem rms_equals_lindelof : frontierRootMeanSquare = frontierLindelof := rfl

/-- **And the trivial bound exceeds it by exactly the Farey order.** -/
theorem trivial_exceeds_lindelof : frontierTrivial - frontierLindelof = 1 / 3 := by
  unfold frontierTrivial frontierLindelof; norm_num

/-- That excess is one factor of the Farey order, matching the coherence deficit. -/
theorem excess_is_coherence_deficit :
    frontierTrivial - frontierLindelof = coherenceDeficit (1 / 3) := by
  rw [deficit_equals_scale, trivial_exceeds_lindelof]

/-! ### The exceptional set -/

/-- Exponent of the number of `n ≤ N` at which the sum can exceed `N^(1/3 + d)`. -/
def frontierExceptionalCount (d : ℚ) : ℚ := 1 - 2 * d

/-- **It is derived from the mean square.**  Values exceeding `N^(1/3+d)` contribute
`N^(2/3+2d)` each, against a total of `N^(1+2/3)`. -/
theorem exceptionalCount_from_meanSquare (d : ℚ) :
    frontierExceptionalCount d = 1 + frontierMeanSquare - (frontierMeanSquare + 2 * d) := by
  unfold frontierExceptionalCount; ring

/-- **The exceptional set shrinks as the excess grows.** -/
theorem exceptionalCount_antitone {d d' : ℚ} (h : d < d') :
    frontierExceptionalCount d' < frontierExceptionalCount d := by
  unfold frontierExceptionalCount; linarith

/-- **It vanishes only at `d = 1/2`**, far beyond the range in question. -/
theorem exceptionalCount_zero_iff (d : ℚ) : frontierExceptionalCount d = 0 ↔ d = 1 / 2 := by
  unfold frontierExceptionalCount
  constructor <;> intro h <;> linarith

/-- At the trivial excess `d = 1/3` the exceptional set still has exponent `1/3`. -/
theorem exceptionalCount_at_trivial : frontierExceptionalCount (1 / 3) = 1 / 3 := by
  unfold frontierExceptionalCount; norm_num

/-! ### The two-sided position -/

/-- The known lower bound's exponent — the resonance method contributes only a subpolynomial
factor. -/
def frontierKnownLower : ℚ := 1 / 3

/-- **The known lower bound already matches the Lindelöf value in exponent.** -/
theorem lower_matches_lindelof : frontierKnownLower = frontierLindelof := rfl

/-- **So the whole open interval is between the mean and the trivial bound.** -/
theorem open_interval :
    frontierKnownLower = 1 / 3 ∧ frontierTrivial = 2 / 3 ∧
      frontierTrivial - frontierKnownLower = 1 / 3 := by
  refine ⟨rfl, rfl, ?_⟩
  unfold frontierTrivial frontierKnownLower; norm_num

/-!
# The logarithmic mean of the squarefree indicator

The `μ²` instance of `LogSumFromCount.lean`: the squarefree count is `mD + O(√m)`, so

    ∑_{√x < a ≤ 2√x} μ²(a)/a  →  D log 2,      D = 6/π².

This is what turns the main term of the `μ²` bilinear sum into the square of the block mean.
-/

namespace RHTower.Sieve

open Finset ArithmeticFunction Filter Topology

theorem squarefreeDensity_nonneg' : 0 ≤ squarefreeDensity := by
  rw [squarefreeDensity_eq]
  positivity

/-- The squarefree counting error, in the general notation. -/
theorem abs_weightErr_moebius_sq_le (m : ℕ) :
    |weightErr (fun n : ℕ => ((moebius n : ℤ) : ℝ) ^ (2 : ℕ)) squarefreeDensity m|
      ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt m + 2 := by
  have hbase := abs_sum_moebius_sq_Icc_sub_le m
  rw [weightErr, weightCount]
  linarith [hbase]

/-- **The logarithmic mean of the squarefree indicator over a dyadic block.** -/
theorem tendsto_squarefree_block_log_mean :
    Tendsto (fun u : ℝ => ∑ a ∈ Finset.Icc ⌈u⌉₊ ⌊2 * u⌋₊, ((moebius a : ℤ) : ℝ) ^ (2 : ℕ) / (a : ℝ))
      atTop (𝓝 (squarefreeDensity * Real.log 2)) :=
  tendsto_block_log_mean_of_count squarefreeDensity_nonneg' (by norm_num)
    abs_weightErr_moebius_sq_le

end RHTower.Sieve
